standard_prerequisites.name: Points of the closure of a subset via nonempty basic opens
standard_prerequisites.use: Characterises membership in the closure as nonvanishing after inverting every element outside the prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: Minimal primes of the image of an injective ring map
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the image contains all minimal primes, which combined with specialization stability gives closedness.

core_obligations: First proof: for a prime in the closure of the image and every element outside it, invert that element and observe the localized ring is nonzero, hence the localisation at the prime is nonzero, so a point of the image below it exists, and specialization stability puts the prime itself in the image (proof lines 9844-9858).

Second proof: replace the source by its image to make the map injective, use that all minimal primes lie in the image, and conclude from specialization stability that every prime lies in the image (proof lines 9860-9865).
proof_roadmap: Prove closedness by a closure computation with basic opens (proof lines 9841-9858).
Give a second proof through minimal primes (proof lines 9860-9866).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map R to S, if the image of the spectrum of S is stable under specialization then it is closed (statement lines 9834-9839). The proof offers two arguments: the first characterises a point of the closure by nonemptiness after inverting each element outside it, reduces that to nonvanishing of a localised ring, and uses specialization stability; the second replaces the ring by the image so that the map is injective and uses that the image contains all minimal primes (proof lines 9841-9866). Each argument converts a topological statement into an algebraic nonvanishing or minimal-prime statement, and the author writes both out. H2.
